messages_body:
Hi Laura,

We started seeing a spike in 502s from the hosted API around 09:10 PT this morning for our production ingestion route (route id: livemart-prod-ingest). Attached are three example request IDs: rQ8f2c, rQ8f9z, rQ8g0a. Error payloads return "upstream request failed (502)". The issue affects about ~4% of requests and is impacting downstream reconciliation jobs.

Can you confirm whether there's a known degradation or if you need anything else from our side? We can provide full request logs if it helps.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Ramos
Platform Engineering — LiveMart
alex.ramos@livemart.com

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and the sample IDs. I'm escalating this to our SRE leads now and have opened an incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/IR-2027-10-18-1.

I've looped in Aditya (runtime SRE) and Ben (customer ops). They'll validate whether this is a service-side degradation or a routing anomaly. In the meantime:
- Please hold off on bulk retries; this can make the symptom worse.
- If you can send a narrow timeslice of full request headers for the three sample IDs, that will speed triage.

I'll post updates here as soon as I have them. Sorry for the disruption.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Laura / Alex — quick update from ops triage. We see a brief window starting 09:09–09:18 PT where a control-plane autoscaler reaction led to overlapping replica assignments for a subset of routing shards (internal tag: shard-split-101). That produced a transient split-routing condition: two replicas attempted to serve the same session and the KV cache divergence caused validation failures resulting in 502s.

What we did:
- Isolated traffic away from the affected pool (usw1-pool-7) and routed to standby pool (usw1-pool-3).
- Forced a graceful drain on shard-split-101 replicas; cleared KV mismatch.
- Rolled back a recent autoscaler heuristic that introduced aggressive shard split timing.

Impact window we see in telemetry: 09:09:42–09:17:55 PT. Peak failed requests ~5.3% of the ingestions in that window. We pushed the routing change at 09:25 PT; p95 and error rate returned to baseline by 09:40 PT.

Attachments: diag-trace-20271018.png (heap/trace snapshot) included for your ops team.

Next steps: postmortem draft (internal) and follow-up with long-term fix to autoscaler heuristics. ETA for a customer-facing postmortem: 48 hours.

— Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Alex / Laura — final confirmation from ops: routing change completed and traffic stabilized. Summary posted to status page and incident record: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/IR-2027-10-18-1.

We've created a short postmortem draft (link shared) and attached the internal PDF for reference: postmortem-draft-20271019.pdf. We'll redact internal debug IDs before the public postmortem.

If you want a short summary for your engineering standup, happy to provide a one-paragraph blurb. Also cc'ing operations to start any billing/credit review if that's helpful.

Apologies again for the disruption — we're treating this as a Sev2.

— Ben Carter
Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the rapid response and the timeline. Can you confirm the exact impact window you will report externally (start/end), and what the expected next steps are for compensation/credits? Our reconciliation runs that failed need a firm timestamp for rerun.

Also, are there any recommended mitigations we should apply on our side (backoff configuration, idempotency keys) to be more resilient to these kinds of routing anomalies?

— Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Final answers:
1) External impact window for your customers: 2027-10-18T09:09:42-07:00 through 2027-10-18T09:17:55-07:00. We'll include that exact interval in the public status update and the customer-facing postmortem.
2) Credits: I've opened a billing review with the accounts team (reference: HB-2027-10-18-LIV). We will follow our standard hosted-credits policy for transient availability incidents and will reply with a proposed credit amount by EOD 2027-10-21.
3) Resilience tips for your ingestion jobs: moderate client-side retry with exponential backoff (start 200ms, cap 3 retries), idempotency tokens on ingest endpoints, and short-circuiting bulk retries during elevated 5xx rate windows. We'll add a one-paragraph recommended config to the postmortem.

Please find the resolution summary attached (resolution-summary-20271020.txt) and the postmortem draft link above. If you'd like a 30-minute call to walk through the trace and the proposed autoscaler changes, tell me a time and I will set it up.

— Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
